#1961. Inglorious Hearts crash as flying Falkirk dismantle Wouter Vrancken's toiling Jambos

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the William Hill Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Read more: Furious Aberdeen fans demand Stephen Robinson axe amid miserable form

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#1956. Spanish footballer, 30, dies after suffering cardiac arrest in sickening collision with goalkeeper which saw match abandoned

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and ELIANA SILVER, SENIOR FOREIGN NEWS REPORTER

Published: 02:34 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 19:08 EDT, 4 November 2026

A Spanish footballer has tragically died after suffering a severe blow to the chest in a collision with a rival goalkeeper during a match on Monday.

Jesus De ​Miguel, 30, of CD Tenerife, had been admitted to intensive care following a horrifying foul by FC Andorra goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono, which led to the Spanish second division match being abandoned deep into stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2.

His football club announced that De Miguel's condition had worsened overnight, with the forward passing away this morning.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

Tenerife, from Spain's second tier of football, confirmed De ​Miguel's death in a statement

Tenerife striker Jesus De ​Miguel has died following a collision during a Spanish second division match on Monday

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De ​Miguel, 30, had been admitted to intensive care following a horrifying collision with Andorra goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono (pictured)

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred (Picture from CD Castellon on Facebook)

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement this morning, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.'

'There are no words of comfort; There is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Journalist Ivan Alvarez reported that Owono, who is also Equatorial Guinea's national goalkeeper, 'is very affected by the situation and that the goalkeeper's intention is to apologise privately before making any public statements'.

UEFA has confirmed that a minute of silence will be held at all their matches this week in tribute to De Miguel.

'We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda,' president Aleksander Čeferin said.

'We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.'

The Royal Spanish Footbal Federation have meanwhile cancelled all domestic matches today.

Tenerife's opponents FC Andorra offered their condolences following news of De Miguel's death, writing: 'With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.'

Football clubs across Spain, including Barcelona and Real Madrid, have led tributes following the news of the death.

'Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times,' Barcelona said in a statement.

Real Madrid also expressed their condolences, stating: 'Real Madrid wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club, and all his loved ones.'

The Spanish Footballers Association also released a statement, expressing their 'deepest sorrow' at the footballer's death.

'His loss leaves a huge void among those of us who shared his passion for football, his commitment to the footballers' community, and his work defending the rights of our fellow professionals,' the statement continued.

'The Board of Directors, all the staff of AFE, and the footballers' community wish to extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to his teammates at Club Deportivo Tenerife. In these moments of immense sadness, we send them all our love, support, and solidarity. You will always be part of our family.'

CD Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel was stretchered off the field after a collision with FC Andorra's Jesus Owono

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

De Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances to help secure the team promoted from the Spanish third division as champions.

The forward had previously helped to secure Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón promotions from the fourth and third divisions, respectively.

CD Castellon also released a statement on Tuesday morning in tribute to their former player, saying: 'With broken hearts and inconsolable grief, Club Deportivo Castellón bids farewell to Jesús De Miguel.

'Words fail to express the profound injustice of this loss. He wore this shirt with pride, celebrated goals with our fans at the SkyFi Castalia stadium, and was an integral part of a story that this fanbase will never forget.

'We extend our deepest condolences to his family and loved ones, offering them our heartfelt support during this difficult time. We also join CD Tenerife and its fans in mourning, sharing this sorrow with them. You will always be one of us, Demi. Rest in peace.'

Last September, another Spanish player died aged only 19 after a collision sent him into cardiac arrest.

Raul Ramirez Osorio, who played for fifth-tier team Colindres, jumped to grab the ball when he crashed into a rival player.

He immediately fell to the ground unconscious where his manager and a nursing student attempted to revive him, before he was taken to hospital.

He suffered a second cardiac arrest on his way there and after two days in the ICU tragically passed away.

And a few months ago was the 95th anniversary of a similar tragedy, involving Celtic goalkeeper John Thomson who died aged 22 after receiving a serious head injury.

During the match in September of 1931, Thomson dived at the feet of his Rangers rival Sam English to stop a ball, before hitting his head on his opponent's knee.

He was left unconscious with a bleeding head, before being taken to hospital, where he sadly died.

Former Rangers star Scott Arfield has been appointed the new player-manager of East Fife.

The former Canada international has replaced Dick Campbell, with the Fifers currently languishing ninth in League One.

The 38-year-old spent the final weeks of last season as Livingston's interim boss but will now get the chance to properly launch his managerial career at Bayview.

Arfield spent five seasons with Rangers between 2018 and 2023, making more than 200 appearances for the Ibrox club.

“It is a highly respected club which has great potential, and it is a privilege to be given the chance to lead it forward.”

“This is an innovative appointment and gives a clear indication of our ambitions going forward.

“I am sure that the arrival of Scott will be welcomed by our fans, who are keen to see an exciting brand of football at Bayview.”

#1952. Liam Scales strike enough to drag Celtic across line in Kilmarnock win

Liam Scales provided a looping finish to earn Celtic a 1-0 victory over Kilmarnock.

The Irish defender hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner in the 26th minute to restore Celtic’s four-point lead in the William Hill Premiership.

Celtic – and Kasper Hogh in particular – otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

The Danish striker finished from seven yards after being set up by Nygren and ran to the standing section to celebrate.

His joy was short-lived as referee John Beaton was summoned to the monitor and gave a free-kick to Killie for Mika Baur’s challenge on Greg Kiltie.

Killie had some good first-half chances and Celtic could not get the two-goal cushion in a dominant second half.

The champions were nearly made to pay in stoppage time, but Ieuan Owen could not make any contact with Erik Ring’s inviting cross inside the six-yard box.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill handed Jota his first start since returning from his 18-month lay-off. The Portuguese winger showed some good touches on the left without making a major impact and made way for the fit-again Yang Hyun-jun at half-time.

A Remembrance Day silence lasted barely 20 seconds, with boos coming from all sides of the stadium. The lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

They would have entered to their team one goal behind had Tom Lowery delivered a more emphatic finish after Owen’s cross set him up inside 40 seconds. Sam Johnstone pulled off a double save to deny the midfielder.

Hogh had another good chance soon after his disallowed goal when Duran played him through, but the former Bodo/Glimt forward’s attempt hit the foot of goalkeeper Nico Mantl.

The Dane soon set up Colby Donovan with a clever backheel, but the right-back fired just wide.

Celtic opened the scoring when Scales ran unchallenged to volley Duran’s cross past a static Mantl from 10 yards.

Killie were very much in the game and Johnstone saved from Michael Schjonning-Larsen before Tyreece John-Jules failed to make the most of a good opportunity.

Mantl saved Nygren’s free-kick and he was a busy man after the interval.

The Killie keeper saved from Duran and the Colombian, Donovan, Hogh, Yang and James Forrest all missed the target from half chances.

Baur had a goal disallowed for offside and Hogh was denied by a brilliant diving block from MJ Kamson-Kamara when Kieran Tierney’s cross fell invitingly.

Mantl stopped Nygren’s penalty after Aaron Tshibola was penalised for handball and the goalkeeper soon denied the Swede again from open play.

Baur went off with a knock before Yang escaped a second yellow card, despite appearing to pull down Nicky Clescenco.

Killie soon got their big chance to level, but Owen could not convert.

#1949. First meeting against a team 20 unbeaten: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Ferencvaros

The first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros will take place at San Siro this evening in the Europa League.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

So, tonight’s contest is an unprecedented one, and it pits two teams together that have made very different starts to their Europa League campaigns.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match.

➤ Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencváros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026-27.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing.

➤ The Diavolo suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11.

➤ Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures.

➤ Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967-68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level.

➤ Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

#1948. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Sloppy Reds wilt in Turkey again as Dirk Kuyt masterminds famous Champions League win against his error-strewn old side

Published: 14:54 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:15 EDT, 5 November 2026

The mad metropolis of Istanbul was the setting for one of Liverpool’s greatest nights, when this storied old club won the 2005 Champions League final down the road at the Ataturk Stadium – but right now fans will be glad to see the back of Turkey for a while.

For the third time in just over 13 months, the English giants have travelled to the bustling hub on the banks of the Bosphorus only to wilt amid the deafening noise of a Turkish football stadium.

They lost twice to Galatasaray last season and now, over the river to the Asian side of the intercontinental Istanbul, Liverpool fell flat at the hands of Fenerbahce – thanks to two Englishmen and a friend-turned-foe in the dugout.

Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown, born in Bradford and Birmingham respectively, both scored for Fenerbahce before Vedat Muriqi scored a winner as caretaker manager Dirk Kuyt, once a cult hero at Anfield, recorded a win in his final game in the dugout.

He will soon be replaced by ex-Newcastle and 101-cap Turkey midfielder Emre Belozoglu but Kuyt will not be forgetting this evening in a hurry in front of a raucous, hostile crowd in the district of Kadikoy.

As for Liverpool, who jetted home straight after the game and were due to land around 2am English time, they and boss Andoni Iraola were just glad to get out of Turkey, probably with their ears still ringing.

It was a poor night for Liverpool as they went down 3-2 against Fenerbahce in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola's side let a second-half lead slip and there were some terrible errors

Archie Brown sunk to his knees in celebration at full-time as the home crowd erupted

Trey Nyoni had scored his first goal in professional football and then Alexander Isak headed home to put Liverpool 2-1 up two minutes after coming on as a substitute but they were undone by sloppy defensive errors.

That will give Iraola plenty to ponder in the coming weeks given his side have conceded nine goals in their last three European games, all to opposition that would not be counted as part of the continent’s best in LASK, Villarreal and now Fenerbahce.

Aside from a UEFA Super Cup triumph over Chelsea at the home of Besiktas in 2019, Liverpool have struggled in this country and their last Turkish delight came against Trabzonspor, who now employ a certain Mohamed Salah, back in 2010.

Fenerbahce and Kuyt celebrated a famous win – as did around 45,000 home fans who produced deafening whistles every time Liverpool had the ball.

It was a true attack on the senses and Iraola’s side felt it, with several passes going astray as Kuyt’s men had the best of the first-half action and were unlucky to go into the break level at 1-1.

Liverpool had gone ahead on 25 minutes through Nyoni’s first goal in professional football, when a header from English full back Brown fell straight into the path of the Reds midfielder, who charged on to the ball like he was Steven Gerrard.

He needed a deflection off defender Kojo Peprah Oppong but cared not a jot as his volley ended up beating former Manchester City man Ederson.

It continued a stellar season for 19-year-old Nyoni, who has had a fairytale week that included a first Premier League start, first professional goal and also talks over a bumper new contract. To say it would be deserved would be the understatement of the season.

Trey Nyoni opened the scoring for the Reds but his goal came in a losing effort

Alexander Isak headed Liverpool back in front after some terrible Fenerbahce defending

FENERBAHCE (4-3-3): Ederson 5; Semedo 5 (Muldur 75), Skriniar 6, Peprah 6, BROWN 8; Guendouzi 7, Kante 7, Yuksek 5; Greenwood 8 (Aydin 89), Lukaku 7 (Muriqi 63, 6), Kahveci 7 (Arturkoglu 75).

Subs not used: Cetin, Gunok, Efe Demir, Mercan, Elmaz, Nene, Mimovic.

Scorers: Greenwood 29, Brown 73, Muriqi 79.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 4; Gomez 5 (Wirtz 66, 6), Jacquet 5, Van Dijk 4, Tsimikas 4 (Kerkez 76); Nyoni 8 (Koumas 85), Mac Allister 7; Munoz 5 (Isak 66, 6), Szoboszlai 5, Ngumoha 7 (Gakpo 67, 6); Barcola 5.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Danns.

Nyoni’s goal, in theory, should have helped Liverpool settle. As it was, it did anything but.

Fenerbahce came out roaring and hit the bar instantly through Irfan Can Kahveci. With the next attack, they were level, just four minutes after falling behind.

Just like Liverpool’s goal, the Turkish side needed a hefty deflection to help them. Greenwood took a free-kick from 25 yards, Jeremy Jacquet turned his back on it and foxed Alisson. Two Brazilian goalkeepers, two wicked deflections that neither could do anything about.

Alisson was the best away player on the pitch in that opening 45 minutes, thwarting Greenwood, the brute force of Romelu Lukaku and fellow former Premier League favourite N'Golo Kante, who is now 35 but still has the energy of the young whippersnapper we all knew and loved.

Iraola turned to his bench with a £285million triple-change and two of them combined just minutes later, Cody Gakpo crossing for Isak to head home his seventh of the season.

But just as when they went 1-0 ahead, Liverpool retreated and invited pressure. A Kante cross was not dealt with by Gakpo and Brown could ghost in at the back post to score.

Then, on 79 minutes, Muriqi thumped home a header to put Fenerbahce 3-2 up and on their way to a memorable night.

Liverpool, who would have taken a huge step towards qualification with a win here, still have work to do.

#1946. Hearts ‘embarrassment’ as furious Vrancken lets rip after Falkirk nightmare

Wouter Vrancken condemned a “ridiculous” first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the William Hill Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Jambos, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a 5-2 victory at Tynecastle.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Jambos, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

Read more: Liam Scales strike enough to drag Celtic across line in Kilmarnock win

“This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,” said Vrancken. “Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

“When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

“It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

“This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,” said Vrancken.

“Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.”

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who made it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time in 31 years.

“I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,” said Bairns manager John McGlynn. “First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

“It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

“We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

“We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

“Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

“Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.”

#1945. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

#1944. Wolves loanee has no regrets about rocky Celtic ride as he steps out of shadows to embrace the spotlight

Sam Johnstone has experienced enough of football's highs and lows to understand that joining Celtic was never likely to be a straightforward undertaking.

But despite a turbulent introduction to life in Glasgow, the Wolves loanee insists he has absolutely no regrets about taking on one of the most demanding challenges of his career to date.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The former England international headed north of the border earlier this summer in search of regular first-team football and a fresh challenge. What followed has been a mixed introduction, with inconsistent results bringing added scrutiny, while adapting to a new team environment has required patience.

His career has been defined as much by patience as it has by perseverance. The Manchester United youth product has spent lengthy spells waiting in the wings for his opportunity, often occupying a back-up or third-choice role, while striving to establish himself as a No.1

Arriving at Celtic has offered a welcome change of circumstances. Rather than being confined to a supporting role, Johnstone has the chance to make the position between the sticks his own as he continues to enjoy a sustained run of games and remind people of the qualities that once earned him international recognition.

There is also the matter of developing relationships with the defenders in front of him. Communication, trust and familiarity are essential for any goalkeeper, and Johnstone recognises that those connections take time to establish.

“I think I've got to get used to them, they've got to get used to me, and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team,” he said. “To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm. It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.”

Having represented established clubs such as West Bromwich Albion and Crystal Palace, Johnstone is no stranger to pressure. However, he has discovered that the expectations at Celtic are particularly intense, arguably unlike anything he has experienced elsewhere in his career.

“Of course it has,” Johnstone admitted when asked whether fluctuating results had affected the mood within the dressing room. “I think the results affect it. This club's not used to losing, and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

“The expectation here, rightly so, is to win. Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation, and the lads know that. We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game. It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people, and honest with each other.”

Ultimately, though, signing for Celtic was an opportunity Johnstone was never likely to pass up. The quality within Martin O’Neill’s squad, coupled with the passion of the supporters and the chance to experience the club's unique atmosphere, made the move an attractive proposition.

“It's brilliant to play for this club,” he insisted. “The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training. When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here. It’s a great team to play in. The lads came up with the goods (on Thursday vs Besiktas], so we keep taking it game by game and go again on Sunday.”

Whether his time with the Scottish champions will provide the springboard to revitalise his career remains to be seen. Asked if the move had given him a fresh lease of life, Johnstone was typically measured in his response. “Let's see, let's see.”

#1943. Rangers turn up heat on leaders Celtic despite controversy in Paisley

A bitterly cold, damp Saturday night in Paisley yielded precisely the sort of calculated, business-like victory that defines title credentials. Under the floodlights of the Marbill Coaches Stadium, Rangers maintained their pursuit of league leaders Celtic with a dominant 2-0 win over St Mirren.

In truth, the scoreline scarcely reflected the visitors’ control of proceedings, a superiority anchored by a dominant midfield display and punctuated by goals from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil in either half.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

This was an exercise in efficiency for Rangers manager Derek McInnes as his side arrived in Renfrewshire looking to maintain their unbeaten away record in the league this season. Making just one change from last weekend’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final triumph over Aberdeen, his side displayed a fluid composure that left the hosts chasing shadows for long periods.

Although Rangers have endured an inconsistent record on previous visits to Paisley, dropping points in three of their last four league outings, their latest success extended a domestic unbeaten run to 12 matches and left them in a confident place heading into the final international break of the year.

St Mirren, under the stewardship of Craig McLeish, had promised a robust, positive approach as they looked to arrest a worrying slide in form that had saw them lose six of their previous eight games. However, the reality for the Buddies was an evening spent largely in a low defensive block, starved of possession and unable to test Ivor Pandur in the visitors' goal until it was too late.

The breakthrough arrived in the 18th minute through a moment of controversy. Left-back James Penrice drove into the penalty area and went down under pressure from a trailing Samuel Ramos leg. While the home support vociferously claimed the new Scotland call-up went down theatrically, referee Nick Walsh pointed directly to the spot.

Naderi stepped forward, ignored the jeers, and showed admirable composure to confidently dispatch the penalty into the bottom right-hand corner, with Jacob Chapman diving the opposite direction. It marked the German’s sixth goal in his last seven games.

Going behind did little to alter St Mirren’s conservative shape as their build-up play lacked urgency, and Rangers continued to dictate the tempo. Their front three of Badredine Bouanani, Kim Minsu, and Kevin Kelsy probed intelligently. The hosts did have a penalty appeal of their own dismissed when Ramos’ header back across goal appeared to strike Naderi’s hand.

The second half followed an identical script, and the definitive blow arrived just after the hour mark. It was a goal engineered by the persistent work of Kelsy who battled fiercely to pick up Olwethu Makhanya’s pass.

His determination allowed the ball to break kindly to Neil, restored to the starting line-up, on the edge of the box and the midfielder side-footed effort took a wicked deflection of Declan John to completely wrong-foot the helpless Chapman, with the ball nestling in the bottom left-hand corner. It gave Rangers some welcome breathing room.

St Mirren did mount a late, spirited assault on the visitors goal, but were denied on several occasions by Pandur. Their best opportunity fell to substitute Eseosa Sule, who met a pinpoint cross from John at the back post. It seemed a certain goal, but the Croatian goalkeeper produced a sublime reaction save to preserve his clean sheet.

Ultimately, McInnes’s men navigated the closing stages with a minimum of fuss, starving the hosts of the ball and suffocating any remaining glimmers of a late comeback. The victory keeps them firmly within striking distance at the summit, a solitary point behind reigning champions Celtic with a game in hand still to play after this weekend.

#1941. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

“We just came back to that last part of it not being clinical enough. Quite ironic, we scored two goals tonight from a penalty kick and a deflected shot at the edge of the box, given all the chances we had, but I actually thought in the main it was no more than we deserved.”

Naderi was once again central to Rangers' attacking efforts, taking his season's tally to nine goals and five assists after confidently dispatching his first-half spot-kick.

McInnes was particularly impressed by the striker's work rate and physical presence, believing the forward has taken significant strides in recent weeks as he looks to establish himself as a dependable option to lead the line.

“I think he's so willing. His first port of call was to make sure he's a handful to play against and I thought he was that,” McInnes stated. “He needs to build that reputation for being horrible to play against, but equally at a club like Rangers you're going to get judged on the goals.

“He's totally shown that he's somebody you can depend on, somebody that can be trusted, somebody that you can rely on to get goals as well as bring in good performances.”

McInnes was equally thrilled with goalkeeper Ivor Pandur, who produced several important saves to preserve Rangers' clean sheet as St Mirren threatened a comeback in the closing stages.

“I think he's been very clean, very controlled with what he does. His distribution is brilliant, he makes good decisions,” he said. “I think there's so much potential in Ivor. With a rotten goalie, you're not winning nothing. He is somebody who we really take a lot of comfort from.

“I've played with goalkeepers who were brilliant and I've played with some who weren't so good and you never ever felt comfortable. With him, we do. He's been a big part of the amount of clean sheets we've had. I thought we worked hard for a clean sheet tonight but there was a spell in the second half where the space got a wee bit bigger and St Mirren managed to get a few opportunities. Thankfully, you always feel he's got that save in him.”

St Mirren have one win from their last nine league games and boss Craig McLeish was left frustrated by the first-half penalty award, questioning the consistency of the decisions made by officials following Samuel Ramos’ challenge on James Penrice.

“My thoughts on the penalty... If that's the criteria for contact in the box, then fine,” he said. “But Kabs [Ismeal Kabia] gets wiped out in the second half after he puts a cross in. I don't even know if anyone looks at it.

“We get an apology after the game at Ibrox for a penalty that we should have got on Kabs again where there was a decent amount of contact on it. I get that if the ref gives it on the field, then it's maybe difficult for VAR to overturn it. I think if he doesn't give it there and then, I don't think VAR gets involved to give it.

“It's a difficult one and it's a frustrating one from our point of view, but there's also bits leading up to it getting to that situation that we need to deal with better. I need to be careful with what I'm saying. It's a frustrating one from our point of view.”

Asked whether he had spoken to Nick Walsh after the final whistle to seek clarification, McLeish replied bluntly: “No, there's no point.”

#1935. Scott Parker's baptism of fire: West Ham fight back from three goals down to earn draw at Cardiff in new manager's first match in charge

Published: 18:32 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EDT, 5 November 2026

Scott Parker's West Ham launched a thrilling comeback from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in his first game in charge.

Jack Moylan’s first hat-trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at half-time and the travelling fans were furious in the away end.

But the Hammers – inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen – fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point for the new boss.

Parker was confirmed as Hammers manager on Wednesday morning – just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked.

Nuno was axed after a run of poor performances and the club opted to bring in a familiar face, with Parker having made 129 appearances for them as a player between 2007-2011.

It was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

Scott Parker took charge of his first West Ham game after Nuno Espirito Santo's sacking

Max Kilman is seen scoring the dramatic equaliser to make it 3-3 against Cardiff

Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Republic of Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shelbourne in May 2023.

The draw extends Cardiff’s unbeaten home league run to 10 games over the last two seasons, while West Ham occupy the final play-off place in eighth.

Nuno’s 13-month tenure had ended after the Hammers had won just twice in six matches and lost successive home games to Southampton and West Brom.

Taty Castellanos had hinted at better times ahead, forcing Nathan Trott into early action after Bowen’s effort had deflected to him.

But the Hammers were behind after Alex Robertson found Moylan in the 11th minute. Moylan advanced to find the top corner of Mads Hermansen’s net with a ferocious strike from 20 yards.

Hermansen tipped aside Calum Scanlon’s cross and Will Fish headed over as Cardiff probed. There was no reprieve for West Ham when Perry Ng curled a ball over a static defence after 36 minutes.

Moylan cleverly slowed down for Morato to bundle him over, a clear penalty.

Cardiff had missed their last two spot-kicks, but this time Moylan was entrusted with the responsibility and sent Hermansen the wrong way.

Angry Hammers fans responded with cries of ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt’, and many of them appeared to be making a swift departure three minutes later.

Jarrod Bowen was a key man for the Hammers as they staged a remarkable recovery

Joel Bagan’s corner cleared Fish at the near post, but Moylan came in behind him to head home his sixth goal in five games, and his 10th of the season.

Parker sent on Mohamadou Kante and Joel Piroe for Soungoutou Magassa and Castellanos at half-time and there was instantly more conviction from the Hammers.

Bowen floated a delicious pass through after 58 minutes, and Mukasa lifted the ball over Trott and in off a post.

The deficit was reduced further seven minutes later when Piroe flicked on Bowen’s pass and Engels slid home his first Hammers goal.

Kante nearly toe poked the ball past Trott before Kilman touched home Bowen’s brilliant cross, and West Ham almost won it through substitutes Ezra Mayers and Tomas Soucek.

#1932. I watched Rangers beat St Mirren and spotted penalty controversy, growing Ibrox influence and big achievement

Rangers returned to winning ways on the road with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren in Paisley on Saturday night, extending their unbeaten domestic run to 12 matches in the process.

Derek McInnes' side had been held to draws in their previous two league fixtures away from home against Dundee and Hearts, but goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil ensured there would be no repeat disappointment at the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The result leaves the Ibrox side just one point behind Celtic at the top of the Scottish Premiership, although the league leaders have the opportunity to extend their advantage when they face Kilmarnock this afternoon.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold in Paisley for The Scotsman and picks out his three main takeaways from the game.

Rangers have now gone 12 matches without defeat in all competitions, a remarkable improvement given the uncertainty that followed McInnes' rocky start to life in Govan. Their success last night was thoroughly deserved but there remains considerable scope for improvement, particularly in the final third.

McInnes has warned that his team are not yet the finished article. There are still familiar frustrations he must continue to address. Rangers' inability to turn promising attacking situations into goals meant St Mirren remained in the contest for longer than they should have, while some questionable decision-making in the final third prevented the visitors from recording a more emphatic winning margin.

At the opposite end, though, Rangers continue to demonstrate the defensive resilience that has underpinned their domestic revival. Six clean sheets in 12 league outings represent a major achievement and provide McInnes with a solid base on which to build from. Olwethu Makhanya was fortunate to escape punishment for a couple of uncharacteristic errors on this occasion, but his defensive partner Emmanuel Fernandez produced a commanding performance to make up for it.

Rangers now have an international break to regroup before returning to Premiership action with a trip to Motherwell on November 21. McInnes will hope his players return refreshed, with the opportunity to build on their unbeaten sequence and address the attacking shortcomings that continue to prevent his side from reaching their full potential.

The game's major talking point came midway through the first-half when Rangers were awarded a penalty following a challenge by Samuel Ramos on James Penrice. The St Mirren man appeared to make minimal contact with the Rangers left-back inside the area, but referee Nick Walsh was quick in pointing to the spot.

Unsurprisingly, the decision did not go down well with the home support and Buddies boss Craig McLeish. They felt the contact from Ramos was insufficient to warrant a spot-kick, particularly given the nature of the challenge and Penrice's theatrical reaction as he went to ground. There was an expectation that VAR might intervene, but after a short review the incident, the official’s on-field decision was allowed to stand.

The award subsequently left onlookers and television pundits questioning whether there had been enough contact to justify the referee’s decision, with Chris Sutton stating in commentary “Penrice has played Nick Walsh like a piccolo.” While Rangers will argue that Penrice was impeded, St Mirren were left feeling aggrieved by a call that had a significant bearing on the contest.

The controversy provided Saints with a legitimate grievance and raised questions about the threshold for awarding penalties, particularly when VAR elects not to overturn the referee's original judgement. One that is sure to divide opinion...

Ryan Naderi has emerged as an increasingly influential figure during a period in which injuries to Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland have left Rangers short of attacking options. The forward has responded admirably, combining his physical presence and willingness to lead the line with an impressive goalscoring return. His six goals and three assists in his previous eight league appearances underline the extent of his recent contribution.

Against St Mirren, he provided further evidence of the growing importance he is assuming under McInnes by putting the disappointment of an early miss quickly behind him to break the deadlock from the penalty spot after 18 minutes. The German was coolness personified in his stuttered run-up before sending he goalkeeper the wrong way. Amid a hectic run of fixtures, his ability to deliver consistently is proving invaluable.

Beyond the numbers, it is Naderi's all-round game that appears to have particularly caught his manager’s eye. McInnes was effusive in his praise of the striker's physicality, work-rate and ability to stretch opposition defences post-match. His willingness to run the channels, attack space and bring others into play offers Rangers another dimension in the final third.

McInnes also revealed that Naderi has been practising penalties regularly in training, with that additional work translating into greater assurance when stepping up under pressure. Having inherited a squad without an established penalty specialist or set-piece take following James Tavernier’s exit, the Rangers boss will be pleased to have identified a player increasingly comfortable taking responsibility in decisive moments. Naderi's conversion was another demonstration of that growing confidence.

Naderi has certainly taken his opportunity to impress and strengthened his claim for a regular starting position. There is still room for improvement, but his relentless energy makes him an increasingly difficult player for McInnes to overlook. The question now is whether he can maintain those level when Rangers' attacking options return to full fitness. For the time being, he is making a compelling case to be one of the first names on the team sheet.

#1930. Rangers away-day concerns give way to renewed optimism as Dan Neil outlines blueprint for silverware

There was something reassuringly uncomplicated about Rangers' 2-0 victory over St Mirren. After a sequence of performances in which attacking promise had not always been matched by defensive security or an ability to put opponents away, this was a night when they got the fundamentals right and the points secured without undue drama.

In Dan Neil’s case, it served as a reminder that Rangers’ away form need not be a source of anxiety. They head into the international break in high spirits and safe in the knowledge that they are within touching distance of Premiership leaders Celtic.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Rangers' recent away performances had exposed a gap between their form at Ibrox and their consistency on the road. Goal scorer Neil acknowledged that concern, describing the win in Paisley as an important response to two disappointing results on their travels in recent weeks.

“It was a good result going into the break,” the stand-in captain admitted. “It was really important that we got that and got back to keeping clean sheets. One of the big things we spoke about before the game, other than clean sheets, is coming away from home and putting in a good performance. The last two away results and performances really haven't been us. We didn’t want it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

“Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. The better our away form is, the better chance we're going to stand [of winning the title]. Every good team just finds a way to win. Obviously we'd like to win by four or five goals every week, but unfortunately that's just not football. I do think it's an area that we can improve on, though.

“These are potential banana skin games. It's important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you've seen that. Our home form speaks for itself, but like I said, the last two away results haven't been great for us. So it was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us.”

The international break provides Rangers with an opportunity to recover ahead of a gruelling winter schedule, although Neil acknowledged that the interruption could also disrupt their rhythm.

”There's definitely pros and cons to international breaks,” he stated. “It's a chance to recharge your batteries a little bit after an intense run of games. But it also kind of halts your momentum a little bit. I think it's important that you take the positives out of the break.

“We can rest and recover ahead of the tough winter months. Hopefully all the boys come back unscathed and have good games with their international teams. I’ll be working hard at the training ground as well as having a few days off and we'll come back ready to fire again.”

There is also a shot at silverware on the horizon. Rangers have five fixtures to negotiate before their Premier Sports Cup final appearance, and Neil is conscious that momentum must be maintained.

“I'm sure we'll relay that message when all the boys are back together,” Neil added. “It's a great chance for us to build some momentum again after a break, going into that final. It's important that we take each test in isolation and not look too far ahead. When the final comes round, it comes round. We've got five really important fixtures before that in which we need to pick up as many points as we can.”

Great chance for the Englishman and the shot isn’t too bad either, but the goalkeeper makes a nice save with his left leg.

Clear elbow on Gila there by Yusuf, so the referee hands out the red card after checking with VAR.

Potential red card for Ferencvaros after an elbow on Gila.

A good effort by Ferencvaros forces Torriani to a nice save.

Quick counter-attack as De Winter’s clearance falls perfectly for the away side, allowing them to play their man in behind.

Worst cross of the season goes to Terracciano. Not even close to finding the players in the box.

Great setup by Ramos but Hutchinson fails to find the back of the net. Perhaps not a brilliant angle but the feeling is that he should have scored.

HUGE howler by Torriani, taking a heavy touch on the backpass to gift Ferencvaros the opener. He shouldn’t have got such a bad pass to begin with, but he needed to do better there.

Pretty clear card for stopping a dangerous counter-attack with no attempt at playing the ball.

Ramos does really well to create some space with a couple of nice dribbles, but his shot is deflected out for a corner.

Pulisic, Ramos and Hutchinson combine to create a first chance of the second half, but the Englishman’s effort hits the side netting.

Back underway at San Siro. Three key subs by Amorim, which clearly show that he wasn’t happy with the first 45 minutes.

😕 Poor first half with more or less no chances for Milan.

🤔 Would you make any changes for the second half? https://t.co/V0EwVlIaug

Milan basically haven’t created anything and Ferencvaros have looked a lot better in possession. Some changes and tactical tweaks are clearly needed, otherwise the away side will find the back of the net after being denied by Torriani so far.

Torriani gets down low to keep out the shot, good save again by the youngster as Milan continue to concede chances.

Terracciano finds Ramos in the box, who heads it down to Cisse, but the shot is not on target. Tough on the volley.

Great chance to put Bartesaghi in a good position on the left, but Rabiot’s poor pass symbolises the first half so far.

Really strange defending from Bartesaghi, trying to shield the ball and then losing out completely. Milan have zero rhythm in their build-up phase.

#1928. Thomas Tuchel reveals why Cole Palmer has been left out of England squad AGAIN

Thomas Tuchel has explained Cole Palmer is still paying the price for missing too many England camps after the Chelsea star was once again left out of his Three Lions squad.

Palmer was left out of the World Cup squad in the summer and withdrew from the group for the extended international break in September and October due to injury.

Tuchel warned it was a ‘missed opportunity’ for Palmer at the time, insisting he ‘misses way too many camps’ with other players moving ahead of him in the pecking order as a result.

Palmer has played almost every minute of Chelsea’s Premier League campaign this term with his injury problems from last season seemingly behind him.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Tuchel made the decision on Friday to leave him out of the squad for upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain with Jobe Bellingham and Fulham’s Josh King named ahead of him.

Speaking on Friday, Tuchel explained King’s versatility was a key reason for his inclusion ahead of Palmer. Morgan Rogers and Morgan Gibbs-White also also vying for the no10 spot with Tuchel explaining the group that impressed him training last month keep their places on merit.

‘It is enough no10s [in the squad] and we stick with guys who were in camp because camp was excellent for the two-and-a-half weeks we had together,’ Tuchel said.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Jason Steele (Brighton)

Defenders: Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

‘The impact of other players was immense and that’s why we stick with the group and all the offensive players. We have Josh King in there but I also want to see him on both wings, he can play all four positions, that is basically the reason.’

Tuchel added: ‘Everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But we are speaking about a player who is not in camp and on the other hand it counts when you are in camp and I said it last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress.

‘It was a long camp, two-and-a-half weeks and the boys who were in the camp built something extraordinary. That’s why the credit and trust goes to them.

‘It’s not personal and we will never assume Cole is not in the mindset to play for his country but the competition is on and the players from that camp keep their place.’

#1926. Former Rangers star lands first managerial job as SPFL club appoint Europa League finalist

East Fife have appointed former Rangers midfielder Scott Arfield as their new player-manager.

The 38-year-old replaces Dick Campbell who was sacked by the League One club last month after a run of eight matches without a victory.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Arfield has been without a club since departing Livingston in May after taking on the role of caretaker player-manager for the final three matches of the 2025-26 season.

The move to Bayview represents a first full-time step into management for the former Canada international, who also had two spells with Falkirk as well as stints with Huddersfield Town, Burnley, Charlotte FC and Bolton Wanderers.

“I am absolutely delighted to be the new manager of East Fife and I cannot wait to get started,” Arfield, who has signed a contract until May 2029, told the club website.

“I feel I am ready to go into coaching after learning a lot from excellent managers during my playing career, and I am grateful to East Fife for believing in me and for giving me this opportunity.

“My aim is now to create opportunities for others and to build a team which will excite East Fife supporters and attract the attention of the local community. It is a highly respected club which has great potential, and it is a privilege to be given the chance to lead it forward.”

Liam Anderson, chairman of East Fife, added: “We are delighted to have agreed a deal with Scott to become our new player-manager.

“This an innovative appointment and gives a clear indication of our ambitions going forward. I am sure that the arrival of Scott will be welcomed by our fans who are keen to see an exciting brand of football at Bayview.”

Arfield, who played for Rangers in the Europa League final four years ago, will take charge of the Fifers for the first time when Peterhead visit Bayview on Saturday. He also hopes to resume playing this month once he regains match fitness.

An East Fife statement added: "The board of directors is grateful to the interim management team of Jim Moffat, Pat Slattery and Brian Easton, who have guided the squad through the recent period of vacancy. Jim will continue as goalkeeping coach, Pat will assist with coaching while injury prevents him from playing, and Brian returns to on-field duties."

#1925. Why Jobe Bellingham received England call-up instead of Kobbie Mainoo

Jobe Bellingham has been given his first England call-up with Thomas Tuchel claiming Kobbie Mainoo’s recent injury problems cost him a place in the latest squad.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder will join his brother Jude for Nations League games against Croatia and Spain having impressed Tuchel and his staff this season.

He joins James Garner, Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly as Tuchel’s central midfield options with Manchester United star Mainoo among the list of high profile absentees which once again includes Cole Palmer and Phil Foden.

Mainoo was part of England’s World Cup squad but did not play a single minute. He was included in the group for the extended international break in September and October but was among a spate of injury withdrawals.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Mainoo has been first choice in midfield under Michael Carrick when available, missing four of his side’s 14 games through injury. He returned to the team against Chelsea last weekend before playing a key role in the midweek victory over Roma.

Speaking on Friday, Tuchel said Mainoo’s injury last month was a key reason behind the decision not to select him with Jobe getting the nod instead.

‘I think Kobbie has had a difficult spell and missed a lot of matches,’ Tuchel said. ‘In the meantime it was Jobe who impressed in the same level of time and that is what we want.

‘The door is always open for younger ones to overtake and make their mark but that is just a sign of the level of competition in central midfield.’

Jobe meanwhile will have the chance to play alongside his brother in games against Croatia and Spain with Tuchel envisaging a more defensive role for the younger sibling.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Jason Steele (Brighton)

Defenders: Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

‘We see him in central midfield, not as offensive as Jude,’ Tuchel said.

‘It’s an incredible achievement for the family and the brothers. I was very happy to give him the call and I saw his excitement straight away in his smile. It was a very nice phone call.

‘We see him in central midfield so he is one of five players who have for central midfield. He is a more defensive player than his brother, good physique good on the ball, very physical player and can keep possession.

‘Now it is on him because we only have Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare for the Thursday match.’

#1924. Premier League issue official statement after Brighton vs Brentford incident

Albion, who can move up to second in the Premier League with victory at the Amex Stadium, lead 2-0 at half-time on Sunday (November 8).

A stunning strike from Diego Gomez opened the scoring after just 15 minutes.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Eight minutes later, Brentford’s uphill battle became even steeper when their striker saw red, following an altercation with Chema Andres.

The Brazilian was found guilty of violent conduct, following a video review.

The Premier League Match Centre’s official statement, on X (formerly Twitter), read: “After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card to Thiago and upgraded it to a red card for violent conduct.”

Explaining the decision on the pitch, referee Michael Oliver said Thiago ‘pushes his opponent in the face with force’, adding: “Yellow card is cancelled and the final decision is red card.”

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann has also had his say.

He told BBC Sport: “Igor Thiago strikes his opponent in the face. The law is clear – unless it is negligible force that is used, like a playful pat on the cheek, this has to be sanctioned as a red card.

"Referee Michael Oliver had no option but to send him off.”

#1921. Burgess Hill Town digest: Isthmian ups and downs, Trophy trip awaits, U19s thriving

It’s a huge chance for the club to progress in a competition that can give teams at step three a dream of that Wembley Arch.

Hornchurch flew the Isthmian flag in the showcase final in 2021 to beat Hereford 3-1.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

National South side Dover will hold all the aces and be strong favourites for the tie. However, Hill manager Gary Mansell will prepare well and his team will give everything on the day.

All connections, including the hordes of travelling fans, will relish the occasion and represent Mid Sussex football with pride and determination.

As for the 2026/27 Isthmian Premier, the league is perhaps at it historical strongest with a clutch of non-league giants all slugging it out. As we have seen over the past few weeks you take your foot off the gas for a moment you get severely punished.

Hill have had hard a fought-win cruelly snatched from their grasp at Wingate and Finchley and been taught a brutal home lesson by the league leaders Enfield Town.

It’s been tough few weeks as Hill have had to travel to Cray, Erith, St Albans, Wingate and Chatham. However, Hill are taking it all in their stride currently sitting in 11th place just a tantalising three points outside the play-off zone.

On Saturday the club travelled to league powerhouses Chatham aiming to right some previous season reversals.

Chatham’s Ben Allen drove home the first goal on 40 minutes from 30 yards. Hill responded early in the second half as centre back Jack Strange headed home a good delivery from Yoan Edoukou.

The game became very frantic as both sides gave 100% effort. Hill forged three or four excellent shooting chances, but Chatham were happy to throw bodies on the line.

On 80 minutes Charlie Lambert was presented with a golden chance but his well-hit shot was saved by the keeper. With fans on the edge of their seats Hill couldn’t quite force the issue as both clubs settled for a point.

Club Captain Keiran Rowe said: "It’s a good point but also an annoying one. We restricted them to very few chances but created quite a few ourselves. We are travelling home feeling we should have won it.

"I am very proud of how the boys have reacted to the Enfield result (6-0 loss). In the last two performances we have worked hard, stuck together and it has been much better. We just need a little piece of luck and we will be away.”

Meanwhile, the Oliva family have become very much part of the Hillians culture. Coach Berty, his wife Steph and son Luca are a major part of the operation dealing with the pathway arm of the club. Hill are lucky to have them.

Over three seasons Berty has demonstrated consistent and powerful progression with the U18s bringing club success and individual improvement. Now 2026/27 has seen the introduction of the U19 academy in association with Haywards Heath College. It’s been an instant hit with players and fans alike.

Berty in tandem with Gary Mansell has been front and centre – the pair act as administrators and managers of the football side.

The team took on Maidstone Academy at the MTC and ran out 8-0 winners, their first victory of the campaign.

Oliva said: “We are very pleased with the win especially the clean sheet, it’s a good day for us.”

As to the bond with Haywards Heath College he said: “It’s going extremely well, we have the squad for training and matchdays on a Wednesday while they receive an education and facilities that are seond to none at the college.

"The lads have access to the gym and analytics. With us they have the opportunity to play competitive football away from the first team environment’ The team now face Ebbsfleet away on November 18.”

Another two unsung Hill heroes also warrant a mention here – kit managers Nat Ellis and Dan Cross. It doesn’t seem to matter how many dirty kits land at Nat’s doorstep she just gets on with it and does a great job – while Dan is on the road delivering washed kits to away dressing rooms across the south-east, and making sure every item comes back. It’s a slick operation.

Hill might be finding Isthmian wins hard to come by right now, but the club are in great shape as we head towards Christmas. Huge opportunities await.

#1919. Hearts unbeaten home record obliterated as swashbuckling Falkirk earn 31-year first

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.
