#1880. Barnsley FC and Daniel Stendel welcomed fun back like an old friend in FA Cup win v Aldershot Town - analysis

As Daniel Stendel sat down to dissect Barnsley’s 7-2 FA Cup win over Aldershot Town, he offered a wry smile.

He had been asked about the two goals his side leaked late in a game that had already been taken well beyond the opposition.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was a question he will have known was coming, and a question most managers would have enjoyed answering to demonstrate their forensic and demanding nature. The word ‘standards’ would have most likely been used.

Stendel, however, had no interest in poking holes in a mostly scintillating performance. And who could blame him?

Barnsley’s campaign has been largely devoid of fun and rife with simmering discontent. With Bonfire Night celebrations spilling over into the weekend, Stendel clearly felt the Reds needed to simply enjoy the sparks.

“We keep the positive things,” said Stendel. “It's normal that I think about the two goals, but I think we analysed a lot in the last couple of weeks about some situations, some games, and why we didn't win the game in the end.

“I think today is time to say ‘good result, we're in the hat for the next draw’.”

Barnsley flew out of the traps at a dizzying pace and the brakes were simply never applied. By half-time, Cameron McGeehan and Vimal Yoganathan braces and a Reyes Cleary effort had Aldershot dead and buried.

McGeehan completed his hat-trick after the break and Rylan Brownlie got in the act, with the latter rounding off the afternoon after Aldershot had twice hit back via Annisuis Lewis.

“It was good to see that we used the spaces that we get, and a goal after a set-piece.

“I think three goals after crosses was good, especially that. It's one thing that we try to change and what we train in training, why we said we have to cross more balls in the box. And yeah, it was good today.”

Toxicity has enveloped Oakwell in recent months and while it has not been Stendel’s doing, it is clear he is relishing the trickling return of some positivity.

His side’s hard-fought draw with Oxford United a week prior evoked nostalgia, memories of a first spell in which supporter connection was strong.

They did not require the same spirit against the Shots but bluntly, it was just nice to see some goalscoring fun. It is a pleasure with which the Oakwell faithful have not been well-acquainted of late.

“We needed this game,” said Stendel. “It's a good opportunity for everybody to prove what we want to do next week and to get some confidence in defence and offence for winning duels, try to do things, cross the ball early, and in the box you can score goals.

“We have tough weekends in the past, and I think it was good for everybody, for the mindset, for the training time next week, for the game, especially before the weekend game.”

Barnsley will host Oldham Athletic in the Jersey Mike’s Trophy on Wednesday (November 11) but it is clear Stendel’s primary focus is on the Brick Community Stadium. That is where Wigan Athletic will entertain the Reds in a battle of two of League One’s bottom four sides on Saturday (November 14).

A battling league draw followed by a thorough dismantling of an inferior FA Cup opponent represents a start - but it would take a league win for the phrase ‘turning point’ to be uttered with any conviction. At present, it can only be whispered.

“I think we play sometimes really well, but we get no points for that,” said Stendel. “You have to score, you have to defend.

“I think it's important that everybody looks for situations that you can score, not only our strikers.

“I think this is important, especially for the next weeks when we have some games against teams around our situation in the table, but also we talk a lot about our defence behaviour, we have to improve that, and I think it was a good step in the right direction today.”

Barnsley: Slicker, Okedina, Gale (Noslin 76), Kay, Larkeche; Johnson (Kelly 63), Connell; Yoganathan, McGeehan (Taylor 71), Cleary (Brownlie 63); Adeyemo (Kirk 45).

Unused substitutes: Ravenhill, Smith, Richards, Alker.

Aldershot Town: Hayes, Dyce (Robinson 60), Oshilaja, Stickland, Harfield (Adom-Malaki 60); Borgnis, Odusanya; Peart (Gilbert 72), Tima, Sandah (Lewis-Evans 78); Abrahams (Lewis 60).

Unused substitutes: Patmore, Matton, Wyllie, Dinanga.

#1878. “It’s about ambition, concentration, desire” – Amorim tears into Milan after Ferencvaros defeat

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim did not hold back on his team’s performance after the 2-0 Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros.

Milan needed a win having lost two of their first three games in Europe, and instead they responded with perhaps their worst performance under Amorim. Lenny Joseph’s second-half brace was enough for Ferencvaros to emerge with three points that their performance merited in truth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was made to rotate again with six changes from the win over Inter, but in the second half the likes of Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Mario Gila and Luka Modric all came on. The end result was the same: frustration and an inability to piece together the required quality.

Amorim spoke to Sky after Koni De Winter offered his opinion that it is a psychological issue for the team. The words from the manager were transcribed by MilanNews.

You issued a warning that today would be complication…

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire. We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight.”

“It’s hard to explain. We simply weren’t ready to move from the derby to this other competition. When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility, and you can’t show up like that. I probably didn’t ensure the team took to the field ready either.”

De Winter says it’s a matter of mentality…

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

“Maybe I did something wrong these past two days, but not mentally. This team had similar problems last year. We have to find a solution. Tonight we weren’t ready, we weren’t brave. If we don’t win, we’ll have to do everything we can to turn things around, and we didn’t see that.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses; we should have won even with those who started.”

“We have to fix this! We can’t just assume it’s going to be like this. We should have done so many things better tonight. Just being better on second balls would have been much better. We weren’t in the game tonight.”

How important is the Europa League now? It’s a complicated situation…

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

#1877. Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EDT, 5 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended  meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

#1875. Everything we’ve done in training was for nothing – Blackwell embarrassed at Crawley Town’s Cup loss at Wimborne

The Reds slipped to a new low as they were outplayed by seventh tier Wimborne Town, who beat them 2-0 in the FA Cup first round – and it was the second straight season Cralwey had gone out at this stage to a non-league side.

Goals from Seung-woo Yang and Cameron Munn secured the deserved win for the hosts, as Crawley were played off the park.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking with club media after the game, interim manager Blackwell said he was ‘embarrassed’. He added: “I’m not very happy with what I’ve seen today, and I’ve learnt a lot today. This was a key game for me because expectation was on the players. I wanted to see how they would react with expectations. And I’m sorry to say I’ve not been impressed with what I’ve seen today.”

The Reds came into this game after good results against Tranmere and Oldham – and were long favourites to proceed to the next round.

Crawley fans travelled in their numbers but left disappointed and deeply unhappy at the performance. Blackwell said “I’ve got to apologise to the Crawley fans. And there were some here and there’s some not very happy fans. And quite right, I wouldn’t be happy.

“This has been a really interesting two weeks since I’ve been here. And what I’m concerned about is the undulation in the performances. That, for me, isn’t good. I’ve told everybody where the club is. They know where it is. And while I’m here, I’ll work my socks off for the club. That’s what I’ll do.

“But the players have got to have a long hard look at themselves. They’ve got to decide whether they want to be playing at clubs like this next year or in the Football League. It’s a simple equation. They’ve got to know and have that desire for me to be professional footballers and want to be in the Football League. It’s as simple as that. It’s not hard to work that out.”

Blackwell had mentioned in his pre-match preview about paying the utmost respect to the opposition, but he didn’t feel they did. When asked about that, he said “No I didn’t. I said to the players if I started, I’d still be there at 10 o’clock tonight. All the things that we’ve tried to do and everything we’ve done in training; everything was for nothing.

“If you can’t follow the plans and you can’t follow the roles and responsibilities and you duck out of physical challenges… they were a team that were physical, we knew that. We didn’t need to fight them. We just needed to play some football. We didn’t do any of it. So, I’m bitterly disappointed with what I’ve seen.”

Crawley’s next fixture is against Brentford U21s in the Jersey Mikes’ Trophy on Tuesday (Nov 10) then nothing until Saturday, November 21, when they take on Fleetwood Town at home, which gives Blackwell some time to get the side’s confidence back up.

He said “We saw a good performance against Tranmere and could have won it. We went to Oldham and won it. Then I see this today. So, I don’t know what I’m going to get in the next game.

“And as a manager or as a coach, it’s a nightmare when you don’t know what the performance level your team’s going to give you. I need consistency in performances. We need consistency as a club. That isn’t consistent, so I’ve got to work out what we can do with it.”

#1873. Jordan Thewlis dares to dream after Guiseley striker is the FA Cup hero against Sutton United

Thewlis' Guiseley had been the better side against a Sutton United team two divisions higher in the pyramid, but had yet to make it count.

When Zac Kennard-Kettle blew his whistle as Jack Tinker tumbled in the penalty area in the 86th minute, the home supporters in a 1,556 crowd roared their excitement. But it soon turned to disappointment when the referee signalled the foul came just outside the 18-yard box.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The free-kick was worked to Thewlis – like Tinker, a substitute – and ballooned into the night sky.

"I think VAR would have given a penalty,” smiled Thewlis. "We probably got... not robbed a little bit, but it was touch and go, wasn't it? You think everything's going against you.

"I think we got booked quite quickly where they might have not. I think the league team does get favoured slightly on occasions."

Thewlis had been denied his moment before. He equalised for Conference North Boston United in a 2019 round two replay against Rochdale, only to miss a huge day out.

"They were in League One," he recalls. "We drew away and then we played them on a Monday at home and lost to a late penalty, 2-1. The draw had been made so we knew we were going, it was Newcastle away.

"That was a bit of a killer, the closest I've come to a third round."

Because four minutes into a minimum of five added to a game already running 21 late because of a medical emergency, Thewlis picked the ball up on the left and bundled his way so close to goal that once the whistle went again, there was no doubt.

"Fair play to the ref for giving the pen because it would have been an easy one to wave away," said Thewlis of Jake Taylor's challenge.

"It was a bit like when we were schoolboys," said the 34-year-old’s manager, PE teacher Ian Richards. "He's won it, he takes it. Cam Wilson's our penalty-taker but Jordan's good from the penalty spot. I was very calm because it was him.

"He's played League Two, National League, National League North. He's made a career on scoring and coming inside like that, weaving through to get a shot off or a penalty."

According to Thewlis: "I just tried to keep my head as clear as possible. The free-kick a few minutes before that, I've sent nine miles in the air. (I was thinking) just don't do that.

"I was confident I'd score. I was confident he'd go the wrong way."

Northern Premier League Premier Division Guiesley’s 1-0 win over fifth-tier Sutton was fully deserved.

"Chances created, shots on target, we were the better team, possession probably evenish, although they might have edged it,” said Thewlis.

Sutton began stronger but their only shot on target was Omar Mussa’s from about 30 yards in the 92nd minute. It was right at Jack Hall.

As the Lions got on top, Elliot Owen missed a good header from a corner and left-back Ollie Brown put an excellent chance laid on by Jack Emmett beyond the far post.

“Usually if you don't take them you can get punished," reflected Thewlis. "But the chances kept coming."

And Richards made good use of a 36-minute half-time.

"I said don't let this affect you," he recalled. "You've got the momentum, try and get that momentum again.

"I talked about how the No 9 (Temi Babalola) would come on to be a bit more direct, which he did. And we picked up where we left off.

"Even though they moved the ball quicker, we looked more threatening. There were a couple of last-ditch tackles by them in the area and a lot of opportunities to score."

The game restarted as more of an arm wrestle. Usually, the last 20 minutes between full-time and part-timers favour the pros. Not here.

"If you get dominated from minute one to 70, 80, you're tired, but we weren't ," argued Thewlis, a property renovator by day.

"We pride ourselves on how hard we work the players in terms of pre-season and we make the training more about quality and high intensity than quantity," said Richards. "And we utilise the squad. I felt a bit of that, a bit of home advantage and a bit of adrenaline got us through."

"There's not many in our league that could put nine on the bench, never mind the quality that we've got," said Thewlis proudly.

Winger Amir Berchil grew in influence as legs tied and in Harrison Hopper had a midfielder to pick him out. He did well to go past Besart Topallaj in the 80th minute, but when the ball came to Kallan Murphy, he slipped. Sent clear in the first added minute, Berchil shot at Brits.

But Thewlis was not going to be denied again.

"I'd rather a winnable one – another National League team," was his answer to the obligatory question of who he would like in Monday's draw. "And at home, it gives us a chance, doesn't it? You start looking at the third round now.

"I'd rather get to that third round. I've never got to the third round."

Neither have Guiseley, beaten twice in the second.

Guiseley: Hall; Odunston, Owen, Mbeka, Brown (Thewlis 78); Hopper, Staniland; Wilson (White 78), Emmett (Tinker 57), Berchil (Iggulden 90+6); Murphy.

Unused substitutes: Roxburgh, Lund, Longbottom, Wadsworth, Sinfield.

Sutton United: Brits; Urpens (Nightingale HT), Kirk, Topalloj, Brookes; Osadebe (Mussa 78), Taylor; Folarin, Knight (Babalola 65), Francis (Ogbonna 65); Carter.

Unused substitutes: Bell, Haigh, Moore-Taylor, Njoku, Amartey.

​Day-night game: The time of year and 36-minute half-time break for a medical incident turned the match into a cricket-style day-nighter with the two halves played in contrasting conditions. But whatever light you looked at it, in, Guiseley were the better team.

Star performers: Ollie Brown missed a golden chance, but was otherwise excellent at left-back and in midfield, Harrison Hopper's passing was tremendous, Amir Berchil's wing-play got better as the gam went on and Jordan Thewlis won it from the bench, but all 15 Guiseley players who took to the field were lions.

Draw: The second round draw is on Monday at 6.45pm on TNT Sports and You Tube.

#1869. Xabi Alonso takes aim at his Chelsea players after shock Sunderland defeat

Xabi Alonso was not looking for excuses after his Chelsea side was beaten 1-0 at Sunderland, admitting they did not defend or attack well enough.

The Black Cats were bottom of the Premier League table with just one win in nine games when they welcomed Chelsea to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

The Blues returned to London with nothing, though, with an Enzo Le Fee penalty the difference between the sides.

There was controversy over the penalty decision, with Levi Colwill adjudged to have hauled down Brian Brobbey, although it looked like both players were pulling the shirt of the other.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders hit out at the decision, telling Sky Sports: ‘For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.’

Alonso was not singing from the same hymn sheet, telling the BBC: ‘I haven’t seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better.’

He added: ‘I think it’s an action where he can defend better. It’s our mistake.’

Alonso was impressed by Brobbey over the game, not just in winning the penalty, but felt his defenders could have done better against the big Dutchman.

‘From transitions out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances, he got the penalty as well,’ he said. ‘But we have been preparing for that, we have tried, we could have done better.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but when you defend better than we did today.’

Clearly the former Real Madrid boss did not like he saw from his defenders and he was also frustrated with what his forwards produced.

It was suggested to Alonso that Sunderland’s physical superiority meant they could bully Chelsea, but the manager said: ‘Not bullied. There’s situations that we could have defended better. Situations that we could have had better advantages in attack.’

#1868. Michael Carrick responds to Man Utd relegation fears after Aston Villa draw

Michael Carrick downplayed fears Manchester United were in a relegation battle after a remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

United will sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League during the November international break after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford.

Aston Villa twice led by two goals but Manchester United produced two spirited fightbacks to avoid defeat and potentially prolong Carrick’s reign as manager.

Goals from Brazilian winger Alysson and Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson put Villa 2-0 up inside five minutes but the hosts were level by half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans equaliser against his former club.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

John McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead just after half-time and the visitors appeared to have the game wrapped up when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth on 53 minutes.

But injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw Manchester United salvage a point and avoid a third successive league defeat.

The comeback rivalled the one United produced in the Champions League against Roma during the week but it remains to be seen whether it saves Carrick his job.

Despite avoiding defeat, the Red Devils slip to 18th in the Premier League after ten games, their lowest position at the stage of a campaign since 1986.

Carrick’s side have also gone eight league games without a win, matching a run they have endured just once before in the Premier League.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’m disappointed that we haven’t won the game,’ Carrick said. ‘We looked the better team for long parts of it and we’re making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we’re giving away.

‘We’re not just giving away one, it’s two in succession that put us in such a difficult position. We did it the other night, we did it again today and have come back into the game and had a lot of the game, could have won it at the end.

‘So I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game. It’s just moments that we need to tighten up on. Individual moments where we’re giving teams goals that we don’t normally get.

‘If we tighten up that, there’s a lot of good in that performance. I thought we should have won the game. But conceding the goals we are is not helping us at all.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

‘We have got to tighten up, it’s pretty obvious to say that. It’s giving us too much to do in games. But I thought we did a lot and feel that we should have won the game.’

Asked whether he feels Manchester United are in a relegation battle, Carrick added: ‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation or the results but we can definitely do something about it.’

Responding to Carrick’s post-match interview, former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said: ‘It’s obviously difficult for the manager. He’s under pressure, no doubt

‘He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician. He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

‘But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

‘What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.’

While Manchester United slipped into the relegation zone, Aston Villa stay 10th after extending their unbeaten league run to seven games.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

PSG's 11-game winning run is the third longest in the club's history, after a streak of 12 between April and August 2015, and then one of 16 between December 2015 and February 2016.

PSG head into the international break sure of their place at the top of Ligue 1, with 23 points from their 10 matches.

“Eleven wins in a row – that's good," Luis Enrique said.

"It's the first time we've done that. As is usually the case against teams who are in a tricky position in the table, it was a difficult match. I think we created more chances than usual, we were looking to score more goals, but they defended very well.

"I'm very pleased, especially when we win this sort of match. Winning this match was special, as it always is when we play at the Parc des Princes."

— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_English) November 8, 2026

PSG have won their last five home matches in all competitions, their longest run in a single season since August-October 2024 (also five).

They have scored in each of their last 54 home Ligue 1 matches (135 goals), the longest such run by a team since Nice between May 1975 and February 1978 (55).

Zabarnyi has scored two goals in five Ligue 1 matches this season, which is already his highest tally in a single league season and one fewer than in his first six campaigns in total.

"We're in good shape, good form, and we just need to continue," Zabarnyi said.

"Everything in the team is working well. We didn't do anything special, we just keep working, keep doing our thing and now is just our time. I've worked a lot and kept focusing, and now I'm playing games, and playing well, I think, and I deserve it."

"You've got to be hard to beat" ❌Roy Keane talks about Manchester United lacking the "basics" pic.twitter.com/TnkdbchtcG

‘We go back to some of the basics. The way they’re starting games, the way they’re coming out for the second half. There are things they can improve on.

‘They’re probably lacking a bit of confidence but if you’re giving up four goals at home, you make it so hard for yourself.

‘When they were on a good run of results last year, the goalkeeper was doing very well, making a lot of big saves, he’s not doing that. Bruno was on fire, he’s not at his very best at the moment.

‘The goalkeeper has to do better. It doesn’t help if your goalkeeper isn’t making saves, that hurts the team a lot.

‘So there are some basic footballing reasons… but to be in the bottom three, playing for Man Utd… this should be hurting them.’

Following the November international break, Manchester United return to action with a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool.

Aston Villa, meanwhile, who stay 10th after twice blowing a two-goal lead at Old Trafford, face relegation battlers Sunderland next.

Davide Bartesaghi worryingly claimed that AC Milan did not show ‘the right attitude’ from minute one of their defeat to Ferencvaros.

Milan went into the match against the Hungarian side needing a win to start correcting what had been a negative course so far in the Europa League, yet they served up probably their worst performance of the season so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Lenny Joseph scored twice in the second half which gave Ferencvaros a memorable night at San Siro, but it was one that their performance merited in truth. The Rossoneri threw big names on in the second half but were unable to break the visitors down, even after they got a red card.

Ruben Amorim didn’t hold back in his post-match interview, while Koni De Winter spoke of psychological issues. Bartesaghi spoke to Sky following the conclusion of the game to provide his assessment on things, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“The truth is, we needed to talk to ourselves. The performance is beyond comment. We went onto the pitch without a good attitude. We ruined what had been a good week. We need to roll up our sleeves starting tomorrow and get to work.”

“We knew it would be difficult, especially in Europe. We lacked attitude, grit, and the desire to fight for second balls, and we paid for it.”

Are there any signs of such performances?

“We knew everything, even about our opponents. We’ve been training well during the week, and we were especially enthusiastic after the derby. The alarm bells went off later, on the pitch. In the second half, we tried to recover as much as we could, but we weren’t able to.”

“We lacked attitude right from the start. We needed to react immediately and not wait to take hits. They created opportunities through our mistakes.

“Starting tomorrow, we’ll lick our wounds and see what went wrong, approaching the next match with the right determination and a different team spirit.”

#1864. Gary Neville names four players who will ‘get Man Utd relegated’ after Aston Villa draw

Gary Neville has slammed Manchester United’s failure to sign any new defenders last summer and says the back-four that finished the remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa will ‘get the club relegated’.

The Premier League giants go into the November international break sitting 18th in the table after Villa twice blew two-goal leads to draw at Old Trafford.

United found themselves 2-0 down inside five minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson took advantage of the hosts’ fragile defence.

Michael Carrick’s side were level at half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans’ 44th-minute strike against the club he left last summer

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Josh McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead with a penalty straight after the interval and the visitors looked on course for a big win when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth.

But Manchester United scored twice in injury-time – substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu with the goals – to salvage a point and avoid sitting joint-bottom during the international break.

Despite two comebacks, United’s current position is their lowest at this stage of a season since 1986, while their eight-game winless league run has only happened once before.

Manchester United finished the Aston Villa thriller with a back-four of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu, and Neville said that line-up would struggle to avoid relegation to the Championship.

‘The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window,’ he said on NBC Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

‘The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

‘They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.’

Gary’s brother Phil, who also enjoyed incredible success at Manchester United as a player, added: ‘The back-four that finished the game – Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

"Should be banging heads!" 😡Roy Keane discusses how Manchester United can improve their form pic.twitter.com/r7JZzj62LD

‘That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League.

‘That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League.’

Despite Manchester United’s grim position in the Premier League, Gary Neville doubts a change in the dugout would improve the situation in the long-term.

‘You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce,’ he added. ‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.

‘You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.

‘None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

‘There are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.’

#1863. Vitoria de Guimaraes vs Porto - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:01, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 22:54

Porto will be looking to maintain their perfect Liga Portugal record when they travel to the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques on Sunday to face a Vitoria de Guimaraes side hoping to build on their recent defensive improvement.

Francesco Farioli's men have collected all 30 points available from their opening 10 matches, putting them five points clear at the top of the Primeira Liga table, while the Conquerors sit 13th with nine points.

Ending a four-year wait for the Primeira Liga title last season was an impressive achievement for Farioli in his first campaign in charge, but Porto have raised the bar further this term by making their best start to a league season since 1939-40.

The Dragons have won all 10 of their opening top-flight fixtures, although they still have some way to go before matching their club record of 13 consecutive victories, set during that historic 1939-40 campaign.

Farioli's side have been equally impressive at both ends of the pitch, with only Benfica (27) scoring more than their tally of 25 in the division, while their four goals conceded represent the league's best defensive record, alongside a joint-high six clean sheets.

Porto head to Guimaraes in confident mood after following up a 4-0 league victory over Estoril Praia with an emphatic 4-1 Champions League triumph over Napoli on Wednesday, extending their winning streak to four matches across all competitions.

The visitors will also take encouragement from their recent record at this venue, having won each of their last eight competitive meetings with Vitoria at the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques and kept clean sheets in their most recent three visits.

Vitoria, however, can draw some encouragement from their improved defensive displays, having gone three consecutive competitive matches without conceding since Lucas Furtado took over between the posts.

After managing just one victory in their opening eight league fixtures and enduring a five-match winless run, the Conquerors edged lower-league Lamelas in the Taca de Portugal before following up a 5-0 thrashing of Maritimo with a goalless draw against fellow Minho outfit Gil Vicente last weekend.

That stalemate in Barcelos leaves Vitoria with two wins, three draws and five defeats from their opening 10 league matches, although it did provide their first away point of the campaign after four consecutive top-flight defeats on the road.

The Guimaraes outfit have been considerably more productive on home soil, collecting eight of their nine league points at the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques, and will hope that familiar surroundings can help them frustrate the league leaders.

There is still plenty of room for improvement in attack, however, as Vitoria have scored just 10 goals in the Primeira Liga this season, with only Gil Vicente (eight) and Maritimo (nine) managing fewer among teams outside the relegation playoff places, although the Conqueror’s defensive record has been more respectable at 10 conceded.

Vitoria de Guimaraes form (all competitions):

Vitoria remain without goalkeeper Juan Castillo, who is recovering from an ankle sprain, and left-back Francisco Dias, who continues to recover from a foot ligament injury.

Thiago Balieiro is also a doubt after missing the draw with Gil Vicente due to a knee complaint, potentially leaving Margarido with the same central defensive partnership of Toni Borevkovic and Ahmed Sidibe.

Furtado is expected to retain his place between the posts after overseeing three consecutive clean sheets, while Arnel Jakupovic could lead the attack again as he looks to add to his two league goals this term.

Porto are expected to be without Chris Smalling (knee) and Vasco Sousa, while William Gomes remains sidelined with a broken ankle.

Zaidu Sanusi could return to contention after resuming unrestricted training earlier this week, while Oskar Pietuszewski's inclusion on the bench against Napoli as an unused substitute suggests that he is nearing full fitness.

Gabri Veiga and Borja Sainz have both scored five league goals this season, although the former heads into Sunday's encounter in particularly good form after netting and providing an assist in each of his last two appearances.

Samu Aghehowa also came off the bench to convert a penalty against Napoli, although it remains to be seen whether the Spaniard will displace Andre Silva in the starting lineup.

Vitoria de Guimaraes possible starting lineup:

Furtado; Strata, Borevkovic, Sidibe, Mendes; Nogueira, Mukendi; G Silva, Samu, Camara; Jakupovic

D Costa; A Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Fernandes; G Veiga, Rosario, Froholdt; Sainz, Samu, Pepe

Vitoria's recent defensive improvement could make this a more difficult assignment than Porto's flawless league record might suggest, particularly with the hosts having collected most of their points on home soil.

However, the Dragons have shown they can grind out results even when they are not at their most fluent, and their impressive record at this venue makes a narrow away victory the likeliest outcome.

#1862. Guimaraes lauds Arsenal’s ‘unbelievable’ Premier League start

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bruno Guimaraes is confident that "unbelievable" Arsenal will continue to keep pushing after they ensured they will sit top of the Premier League for the international break.

Arsenal earned a 1-0 win over Hull City on Saturday – thanks to Martin Odegaard's goal – to pull six points clear of challengers Manchester City, who failed to close that gap after losing to Nottingham Forest.

The Gunners have 27 points from their opening 10 Premier League games this season (W9 L1); only Chelsea in 2005-06, City in 2011-12 and 2017-18 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have had more to begin a campaign in the competition (all 28).

They have won each of their last five matches in the Premier League, each coming since the extended international hiatus in September and October.

Prior to that break, Arsenal had suffered a disappointing 3-0 loss to Brighton, but Guimaraes noted how important it was for them to go into this one on a more positive note.

"We had a tough game; they [Hull] made it feel so difficult for us, but it's impressive numbers," said Guimaraes.

"I'm happy for myself, for the team. We'll keep going. We've been unbelievable.

"The message for us was clear in the dressing room. The last time we had a break, we lost to Brighton in one of the worst games of our season.

"The message here was to leave in a good way and go to our internationals happy."

Arsenal have kept a clean sheet in seven of their opening 10 Premier League games this season; only Birmingham City in 2003-04, Chelsea in 2004-05 and Manchester United in 2017-18 have had more at this stage (eight).

They are also on a 10-game winning streak at home in all competitions, only enjoying a longer run under Mikel Arteta in November 2022 (12).

Guimaraes was key to helping Arsenal past Hull, having the most touches (111), successful passes (86/95) and winning the most tackles (2/3).

"He's much better. He had a massive impact; he's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level," Arteta said of Guimaraes.

"That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room. He owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come."

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester United play host to Aston Villa this afternoon knowing that they must win this match in order to keep Michael Carrick in his job.

The under-fire head coach avoided the sack after two heavy defeats against Como and Bournemouth - 4-1 and 3-0 respectively - a fortnight ago, and he was kept in-post for the visit to Chelsea, which United also lost 2-0 at Stamford Bridge.

It meant that Carrick’s men had gone nine games without a victory in all competitions, a run stretching back to late August.

Immense pressure was piling on the former midfielder, with the majority of supporters expecting his dismissal after the thrashing by the Cherries at Old Trafford, but it was reported that the club hierarchy wanted to reassess his position during the November international break.

As such, it gave him the 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League, and it gives him this encounter against a rejuvenated Aston Villa, who are now five league games without defeat.

Unai Emery oversaw a 3-1 win against Viking last time out on the continent, while they stunned Manchester City 2-1 at Villa Park in their most recent league outing.

#1860. The 'family football club' now being promoted by unlicensed gambling and an 'international adult star': Leicester City fans rage against team's choice of sponsor after two relegations

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 05:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 05:24 EDT, 5 November 2026

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Online casino company BC Game, who has been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season, announced its partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this week.

The promotional video, which was laced with innuendo and featured Elfie receiving a package from a delivery man containing her partnership contract, was accompanied with the caption: 'Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin.'

The Foxes Trust has reacted angrily to the shirt sponsor’s association with Elfie, who has also built a following in Esports and competitive online gaming communities.

In a furious statement titled 'BC Game - It gets worse', the fan body said: 'Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the Trust's dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.

'BC Game have now announced a new partnership with "international content creator and Esports personality" Eva Elfie... who just happens to be an international porn star.

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador

Casino firm BC Game has been Leicester's primary shirt sponsor since the 2024-25 season

Welcome to BC Game @EvaElfie! Let the fun begin 😏 pic.twitter.com/xzLJ4uBOx7

'From the moment the Club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. Our first article in July 2024 said that "It doesn't feel like who LCFC are to have a gambling website on our shirts and seems to be another step away from our well run family club reputation".

'The Club has not only partnered with a gambling company, but chosen one that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins, and allows clients to "game" using cryptocurrencies.

'Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

'Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?

'Our end of season survey showed 73% of fans felt negative about the relationship, and only 5% were content with it.

'As always our message is, if you're purchasing an LCFC replica shirt, opt for one that doesn't have the BC Game logo on it.'

BC Game, which The Foxes Trust claim has failed to respond to questions about its funding and legitimacy, lost its UK operating licence in December 2024 and has since shifted its focus to overseas markets.

Focusing on Elfie's esports portfolio in his announcement, BC Game chief executive Ali 'Ako' Muhanned said: 'Eva has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community through genuine passion and consistent content creation.

'At BC.GAME, we want to work with creators who understand how to entertain, connect with audiences in real time, and bring positive energy to our players. Her live streams are dynamic and engaging, making her a natural fit as we expand our footprint across esports and interactive entertainment.'

Elfie, who has 4.8million followers on Instagram, also released her debut single 'Fairyland' last month.

Since partnering with BC Game, the Foxes have plummeted down the football league, suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too

BC Game lost its licence to operate in the UK in 2024 and now targets overseas markets

Leicester, who famously won the Premier League against all odds in 2016 and lifted the FA Cup in 2021, were docked six points for breaching spending rules during last season's dismal Championship campaign and failed to survive the drop.

Today, the East Midlands club sit 10th in League One after 13 matches, winning five, losing four and drawing four.

When the partnership was first announced in 2024, Leicester City chief executive Susan Whelan said: 'We welcome BC Game to Leicester City – an opportunity to work with an innovative partner in a new category for the Club.

'As a leading global operator in a rapidly evolving environment, BC Game already have a history of successful relationships in sport and we look forward to the development of a mutually beneficial partnership.

'The ability to attract high-value partners upon our return to the Premier League is vital to our determination to re-establish Leicester City among the game’s elite, to continue to invest in a competitive squad and to ensure the best possible experience for our supporters.'

#1858. Rio Ave vs Braga - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:21

Braga will be looking to secure back-to-back league victories for the second time this season when they travel to Vila do Conde on Sunday to face a struggling Rio Ave side.

An emphatic win over Famalicao on November 1 lifted Franclim Carvalho's men to eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 14 points from 10 matches, while the hosts have managed just two league victories and currently sit 16th.

Despite finishing in the top four last season, Braga missed out on a Europa League place after second-tier Torreense secured the spot by stunning Sporting Lisbon in the Taca de Portugal final, meaning the Archbishops would have entered this campaign targeting a return to the top three and more secure continental qualification.

However, the Arsenalists find themselves six points behind fifth-placed Arouca after winning just four of their opening 10 league fixtures (D2, L4), although they ended a three-match losing run in the Primeira Liga with a commanding 3-0 victory over Famalicao last weekend.

That result offered some measure of revenge after Braga suffered a penalty shootout defeat to the same Minho rivals in the Taca da Liga four days earlier, while also giving Carvalho his first top-flight win since succeeding the sacked Carlos Vicens in mid-October.

Carvalho, whose first victory in charge came against Gent in the Conference League, also guided his side to a goalless draw away to Aarhus in midweek, meaning the Arsenalists have now gone two consecutive matches across all competitions without conceding.

However, there is still room for improvement in attack, particularly after Braga failed to score in Denmark despite registering 26 shots, including nine on target, while only Gil Vicente (eight) have scored fewer than the Archbishops' 12 league goals among teams currently in the top 12.

The Arsenalists’ attacking shortcomings have been particularly evident away from home, where they have drawn a blank in each of their last five matches across all competitions and gone without a victory in that period, losing three times, including a 1-0 defeat to Nacional on their most recent league trip.

Rio Ave, meanwhile, have struggled to find consistency since Vasco Seabra took charge, winning once and losing twice in his three league matches after replacing Sotiris Silaidopoulos in October.

Seabra began his tenure with a 3-2 top-flight win over Nacional, but despite beating lower-league Louletano in the Taca de Portugal, his side suffered a 4-0 league defeat to Famalicao before losing 2-1 to Academico de Viseu last weekend, despite Miguel Patricio opening the scoring.

Defensive problems have been a recurring theme for the Vila do Conde outfit, who have conceded a league-high 23 goals this season, at least four more than any other side in the division, while their attack has offered little relief after finding the net just nine times.

The Vilacondenses' defensive frailties have been particularly apparent on home soil, where they have conceded multiple goals in each of their five league matches this term, recording just one win and a draw alongside three losses.

Rio Ave can, however, take some encouragement from their recent home meetings with Braga, having avoided defeat in each of the last three, including a 2-1 victory when the sides last met in Vila do Conde in March 2025, while their most recent encounter at the venue ended in a 2-2 draw in August 2025.

Rio Ave goalkeeper Cezary Miszta (back) and defender Nelson Abbey remain unavailable, while Pedro Amaral is a doubt after missing each of the last three league outings.

Enner Van der Gouw was preferred to Vitor Hugo between the posts last time out and could retain his place, while Patricio is also expected to feature again after getting on the scoresheet in that encounter.

Andre Ntoi picked up a red card in stoppage time last time out and is expected to serve a suspension, leaving him unavailable for Sunday's contest.

Braga are expected to remain without Sikou Niakate, who is working his way back from a lengthy Achilles tendon injury that has kept him sidelined since April.

Gabriel Silva is also a doubt after missing the last three matches, although Bright Arrey-Mbi appears to have returned to full fitness after making a brief appearance in the midweek match against Aarhus.

#1855. Santa Clara vs Gil Vicente - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 06 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 21:32

Santa Clara will be looking to strengthen their position in the upper echelons of the Primeira Liga table and move within one point of second-placed Benfica when they take on Gil Vicente on Sunday.

The Gilistas have also made an encouraging start to the campaign, but they journey to the Estadio de Sao Miguel aiming to arrest their recent dip and secure a third consecutive away victory in the league.

Santa Clara turned in a comprehensive team display to return to winning ways last Sunday as they edged out Maritimo 2-0 when the two sides squared off at the Estadio do Maritimo.

While Maritimo squandered several clear-cut scoring opportunities, Tiago Ribeiro and Vinicius Lopes found the back of the net in either half to fire Santa Clara to victory, leaving the hosts to rue their poor finishing.

Head coach Petit will be delighted with the result at the Estadio do Maritimo, particularly after a difficult two weeks, with the Azoreans suffering a 3-2 extra-time defeat against Mafra in the Taca de Portugal third round on October 18, eight days before losing 2-1 at home to Benfica to record their first Primeira Liga defeat of the season.

Having finished 13th in the league last season, their lowest league rank since their relegation in 2023, Santa Clara have taken giant strides this season, picking up six wins and three draws from their opening 10 games to sit fourth in the Primeira Liga table, level on 21 points with third-placed Sporting CP.

Key to Santa Clara’s promising start has been the solid job at the defensive end of the pitch, where they are one of the most disciplined sides in the divisions, conceding just six goals and keeping five clean sheets so far — only league leaders Porto have conceded fewer (4).

On the other hand, Gil Vicente failed to arrest their slump in form last weekend when they were held to a goalless draw by Vitoria de Guimaraes at the Estadio Cidade de Barcelos.

Having opened October with three consecutive victories, including a 3-2 extra-time victory over Uniao Santarem in the Taca de Portugal third round on October 14, Gil Vicente have since endured a downturn in form, going three straight games without a win (1D 2L), a run which saw them crash out of the Taca da Liga courtesy of a 4-1 hammering at the hands of Benfica on October 29.

Despite their recent struggles, Gil Vicente have plenty of positives to draw from, having picked up four wins and three draws from their 10 Primeira Liga games to collect 15 points and sit seventh in the league standings.

Having picked up back-to-back victories over Moreirense and Braga in their last two Primeira Liga away games, Luis Pinto’s men will be relying on their recent improvement on the road as they look to get back on their feet this weekend.

However, a daunting away challenge awaits Gil Vicente at the Estadio de Sao Miguel, where they are on a run of four consecutive defeats and have failed to win each of their last eight visits since a 2-0 victory in September 2015.

Santa Clara will have to cope without Portuguese midfielder Pedro Ferreira, who is set to sit out his second consecutive game after sustaining an injury against Benfica on October 26.

He is joined on the Azoreans’ injury table by 25-year-old defender Matheus Araujo, who continues his return to full fitness after suffering a severe knee injury last December.

Meanwhile, Gil Vicente remain without the services of 21-year-old midfielder Mohamed Bamba, who has been out of action since January due to a severe knee injury.

Jose Silva was forced off injured late in the game against Guimaraes last time out and the 21-year-old defender is out of contention for the trip to Estadio de Sao Miguel, while Frenchman Arthur Tchaptchet also continues his spell on the sidelines.

#1854. Le Bris: Sunderland reconnected with identity in Chelsea win

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Regis Le Bris was pleased to see Sunderland's "reconnection with our identity" as they fought hard for a 1-0 victory over Chelsea on Sunday.

Sunderland ended a seven-game winless run in the Premier League thanks to Enzo Le Fee's 36th-minute penalty, and moved off the foot of the table.

It was an important return to form ahead of the international break, with the players booed off following a 2-0 loss at home to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday.

They were compact and frustrated Chelsea throughout and even went close to adding to their tally through Wilson Isidor and Chemsdine Talbi in the closing stages.

"It was important before the international break to win again, so the three points are crucial in the league but also the reconnection with our identity and our fans," head coach Regis Le Bris told Sky Sports.

"The more we play this style of play, the more the fans support us. It is like a cycle that helps the energy grow inside the stadium. [The game] was really good. I'm happy for the three points, but there's still a long way to go."

That winning feeling is BACK https://t.co/Wdlm7HIrRU

— Sunderland AFC (@SunderlandAFC) November 8, 2026

Sunderland have now won three consecutive matches against Chelsea for only the second time in their history, having last achieved the feat between December 1999 and March 2001.

Le Fee was proud of the team for getting back on track, but he insisted there would be no celebrations while they remain in the relegation zone.

"This type of win shows our togetherness. It's most important to keep going, also for the fans to see us fighting like this. A big, big, big three points," said Le Fee.

"We know that if we fight well and win our duels, the crowd will be even more intense. That's what we need. The first point where we wanted to be good was fight and belief. Everyone in the dressing room believes we can come back.

"We know in football there can be tough moments, there can be better moments – but to have the best moments you have to suffer sometimes. We will keep fighting until the end, and the game showed that we are in a good way.

"It's difficult when you are in a bad moment; you have the feeling that everything is really fragile. You can't leave even one per cent of concentration. You have to stay focused until the end, even when you are tired.

"No [celebrations]. We are really happy. We are still near the bottom of the league. We have the international break to rest a bit. It's good because we won. We have to do more and more every single match."

#1852. GdS: A ‘true disaster’ – scrutiny intensifies as Milan sink to new low in Ferencvaros loss

AC Milan fell to a third Europa League defeat in four games last night at San Siro, losing against Ferencvaros who maintained their perfect start.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by asking the obvious question: what is the real Milan? Is it the aggressive, focused and at times dazzling side seen in the derby at the weekend, or the listless, disjointed, and sterile team witnessed yesterday against Ferencváros?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In all likelihood, the real Milan are both – doomed, partly due to structural limitations, to oscillate between positive performances and lacklustre displays. To be clear, the Rossoneri won’t get far in any competition this way, as there can be no ambition without consistency.

Their last six matches have been a constant see-saw between victory and defeat. On only one of five occasions have Milan managed to come back from a deficit, a sign of a profound struggle to react.

Yesterday, their Europa League campaign became dangerously complicated: direct qualification for the next stage is now little more than a pipe dream, and even reaching the play-offs is hanging in the balance.

As things stand, Milan would be eliminated, and the schedule includes a daunting away trip to face Olympiacos and a home match against Sunderland, followed by two theoretically easier fixtures. The ‘Version A’ of Milan would have no trouble finishing in the top 24, but ‘Version B’ risks falling short.

One must also ask how much they truly care about the Europa League. While it is true that the squad lacks depth and injuries provide a valid excuse, Amorim’s team selections made it clear that Sunday’s away match in Genoa was considered the higher priority.

Yet, making such choices hinders growth. So far in Europe, the Diavolo have delivered three embarrassing performances in four games in Europe. It is a hard pill to swallow, but this is Milan: an international competition cannot be treated like a midweek friendly.

The match against a very good Ferencváros side was handled poorly: a terrible approach, an overly convoluted tactical set-up (even accounting for absences, which must be considered but do not justify such absolute mediocrity), and a complete lack of intensity.

It was as if the players were still suffering from a hangover following their derby celebrations. Amorim opted for a 4-2-3-1 formation, tasking Jashari with orchestrating play, while relying on the pace of Hutchinson and Cissé to disrupt the disciplined Hungarian defence.

The problem, however, was that there was no bow from which to launch those arrows. Jashari once again displayed a concerning lack of personality. Borbely assigned Bero to mark him, and that move alone was enough to reduce the Swiss player to performing only the most basic tasks, which he executed poorly.

Another issue in the build-up phase was the advanced positioning of Rabiot, who was drawn too far toward the final third, making him easy to shield. Unlike in the derby, he found himself receiving the ball with his back to the goal, almost always forcing him to pass backward.

Rabiot’s true value lies in his box-to-box quality: mobility is essential to maximizing his strengths, yet yesterday he was effectively caged by Amorim’s tactical design. Then there is Ramos, who touched the ball just three times (yes, three) in 30 minutes, despite the team holding 68% possession.

What is the point of maintaining possession if your best player remains on the periphery of the match and your centre-forward is never provided with a service? It was fortunate for Milan that, in the first half, Joseph displayed the worst of his repertoire, squandering two prime opportunities.

Realising the issues, Amorim tried to jolt the team into life by bringing on indispensable starters (Pulisic, Moreira and Gila) and dropping Rabiot deeper. It yielded no positive results, as the team’s build-up play remained predictable and their defense lacked cohesion.

Joseph made amends for his first-half finishing errors by scoring twice into an empty net. The first goal was gifted by a reckless back-pass from De Winter that Torriani failed to control; the second coming on a counter-attack, set up by an intelligent touch from Zachariassen.

Meanwhile, Milan’s first shot on target didn’t arrive until the 36th minute of the second half, courtesy of Hutchinson. By that point Ferencváros were down to ten men following Yusuf’s sending-off, and Amorim had deployed both Modrić and Camarda.

The coach opted for an improbable 4-2-4 formation with Moreira playing as a left-back. It was a move born of resignation, or rather, desperation. Which version of Milan will show up at Marassi on Sunday? It’s a question that naturally piques one’s curiosity.

#1851. Rennes vs Lille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 06 Nov 2026 21:33

Rennes welcome Lille to Roazhon Park on Sunday afternoon in round 10 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Rouge et Noir fell to a disappointing 5-2 defeat against Nice at the Allianz Riviera, while Les Dogues snatched a late 1-0 win over Lens on home soil.

After agonisingly falling short of ending their six-year UEFA Champions League absence last season, losing 3-1 to Marseille on the final weekend to finish just two points outside the automatic qualification places, Rennes will be fairly content with how they have begun their latest Ligue 1 campaign.

Franck Haise’s men started the season in emphatic fashion, claiming victory in three of their opening four league games to sit joint top of the Ligue 1 table in the middle of September, but having picked up just six points from their five games since, Sunday’s hosts have slipped to fifth and have just one win in their latest five matches in all competitions.

Despite boasting an unbeaten start to their endeavours on the continent, Les Rouge et Noir will be slightly disappointed with their position in the UEFA Europa League table too, with Haise’s side currently 17th in the standings after drawing three of their opening four fixtures.

Having failed to win any of their previous seven encounters with Lille at Roazhon Park, dating back to a 3-1 triumph on the final day of the 2018-19 season, Rennes will be desperate to rediscover their winning touch this Sunday by ending that barren run and returning to form.

Following a much improved 2025-26 Ligue 1 campaign in which they finished third and booked their place in the Champions League, having only managed Europa League qualification the year prior, Davide Ancelotti will be extremely happy with how his side have started the current season.

With just one league loss so far, falling to a narrow defeat against Nice at the Allianz Riviera in September, Les Dogues have accumulated 18 points from their nine matches and sit second in the Ligue 1 standings, behind only back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain.

Over that span, Lille’s greatest strength has undoubtedly been their defensive solidity, with Sunday’s visitors keeping an impressive five clean sheets and conceding just six goals, a tally bettered by no other side inside France’s top three divisions.

Although much like their opposition, Les Dogues will be feeling extremely underwhelmed with their performances in Europe, as Tuesday evening’s goalless draw with Danish side Bodo/Glimt marks the first point Ancelotti’s men have earned in the competition this season, leaving them only above Slovan Bratislava at the foot of the Champions League standings.

However, having won three of the previous four meetings with Rennes, including an important 2-1 victory when they travelled to Roazhon Park in March, Lille will be confident of putting their European woes behind them on Sunday afternoon by claiming another three points in Ligue 1 and pushing towards Les Parisiens at the summit of the table.

Having netted seven goals in as many Ligue 1 games to start the season, Rennes will be hoping that Esteban Lepaul can finally make a return this weekend from an ankle injury that has kept him out of the previous month.

After missing Les Rouge et Noir’s previous league outing against Nice with a thigh issue, Brice Samba was back between the sticks during the week and is likely to start behind a back five including Bryan Reynolds, Charlie Cresswell and Mahamadou Nagida on Sunday.

Scoring three goals in his latest four matches in all competitions, Senegalese striker Boulaye Dia has stepped up as the hosts’ main goal threat in Lepaul’s absence and will be looking to add to his campaign tally of four Ligue 1 strikes against Lille.

Portuguese defender Tiago Santos and 24-year-old Moroccan Hamza Igamane are Lille’s only two confirmed absentees as they continue their recovery from cruciate ligament injuries, however the latter is expected to return in the coming months.

It remains to be seen whether Japanese forward Ayase Ueda features on Sunday after missing the previous month with a foot injury, though Ancelotti is likely to opt for either Olivier Giroud or Hakon Haraldsson through the middle regardless.

Algerian midfielder Nabil Bentaleb also missed Tuesday’s trip to Bodo/Glimt due to illness, making him a doubt for the weekend.

However, on a more positive note for the visitors, French defender Tanguy Nianzou is back available for selection on Sunday after serving a red card suspension against Lens and is almost certain to slot alongside Alexsandro at the back.

Samba; Reynolds, Ait Boudlal, Cresswell, Rouault, Nagida; Thomasson, Rongier, Camara; Dia, Tamari

With both sides enjoying promising starts to the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign, Sunday’s clash is bound to be one of the highlights of the weekend and could easily go either way.

However, despite their recent struggles in the Champions League, it is extremely difficult to ignore Lille’s current surge towards the Ligue 1 summit, and we are backing them to maintain the pressure on PSG by collecting all three points this weekend.

#1850. Tottenham get new red card review as Leeds defender escapes punishment

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Jayden Bogle should have been shown a red card during Leeds United’s win over Tottenham, says former Premier League referee Keith Hackett.

As Spurs’ three-game winning streak was snapped on Saturday afternoon, the biggest talking point came shortly before half-time when Mathys Tel was eventually forced off after being on the receiving end of a strong challenge from Jayden Bogle.

Replays showed the the Leeds defender had landed his studs on the Frenchman’s left Achilles, but - to the surprise of many - avoided any punishment from referee John Brooks.

In fact, VAR reviewed the challenge for around four minutes and ultimately deemed it did not meet the threshold for serious foul play.

Standard Sport understands Spurs are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send off Bogle, writing to refereeing body, Pro Ref, for an explanation.

Meanwhile, upon reviewing the incident himself, Hackett believes the nature of the challenge should have resulted in a red card.

“This challenge should frankly always be red carded,” he said in a post on X, formerly Twitter.

“The Achilles is a very vulnerable area and the safety of the player must be taken into account.”

On the incident, though, Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi said he still had full confidence in VAR and insisted his side could not blame the officials for the result at Elland Road.

“No, I have big confidence in the referee,” De Zerbi said when asked if he would have wanted referee John Brooks to go to the monitor to look at Bogle’s challenge.

“Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.”

#1849. Arsenal 'should have been awarded a penalty' as Mikel Arteta gets clarity after Hull win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has received some clarity over the offside law after Arsenal were denied a penalty in their win over Hull.

On a day of controversial refereeing decisions in the Premier League, the incident in question at the Emirates Stadium occurred in the first half when Kai Havertz was pulled to the ground inside the box.

The German’s appeals was initially ignored and play was allowed to continue before a sudden halt was called to allow referee Farai Hallam to go to the monitor and review the replay.

While Hallam announced that a foul had been committed by Hull defender Nobel Mendy, Arsenal were NOT awarded a penalty because Havertz was in an offside position.

Now, as the rules regarding such incidents are ambiguous, Arteta has called for clarity as one interpretation is that Havertz was not committing an offside offence due to not “attempting to play the ball or challenging an opponent for the ball”.

“I don’t know, I haven’t watched it back,” the Arsenal manager said in his post-match press conference.

“I didn’t watch it back so I don’t have to lie to you guys. I was surprised, because when they sent the referee to the monitor the bench was telling me that it’s a clear penalty, it’s pulling.

“I know they decided not to because the starting position of Kai was offside, so I don’t know what the interpretation is. I’m sure they will make that clear to understand it.”

Former Premier League referee chief Keith Hackett has attempted to clear up the situation by posting on X, formerly Twitter: “The Offside Law is clear and a penalty kick should have been awarded.”

Ultimately, the confusion over whether Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty was not made into a bigger talking point after the game as Martin Odegaard broke Hull’s resistance in the 72nd minute.

That result, coupled with Manchester City’s loss to Nottingham Forest, means the Gunners have a six-point lead at the Premier League summit.
